A Russian military Mi-8 helicopter entered Polish airspace on September 23 at 11:08 a.m., the operational command of the Polish army said.
The helicopter, flying from the Kaliningrad region, crossed about 300 meters (984 feet) into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds, the Polish military said.
Poland scrambled fighter jets and put ground forces and equipment on alert. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense,” the command said.
Russia has not yet commented on the incident.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on September 17 that Russia is planning “hybrid” strikes using missiles and drones against countries that support Ukraine. He claimed that “there is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles may fly into the territory of one or more NATO countries on the eastern flank, even cause destruction.”

Igor Vasilyev, director general of Patriot Park, has been detained on suspicion of accepting a bribe classified as especially large under Russian law, law enforcement sources told TASS.
Fontanka first reported Vasilyev’s detention. A source told the outlet that the case involves 80 million rubles in bribes. Two of Vasilyev’s deputies were detained before him.
Vasilyev took over at Patriot Park in March 2026. One of his predecessors, Vyacheslav Akhmedov, also faced criminal prosecution: He was detained in 2024 and sentenced to five years in prison in 2025. Akhmedov was convicted of taking part in the theft of 25 million rubles. The money was officially allocated for construction at Patriot Park but was actually used to build a house for former Deputy Defense Minister Pavel Popov.

Russia has brought its first known treason case based on tax payments to Ukraine
October 5, 2026, 7:32 pm
Source: Mediazona
Businessman Oleg Varyukhin, who traveled to Russia after living in Ukraine for 27 years, has been charged with treason for paying Ukraine’s mandatory military levy into its state budget, Mediazona reported.
Varyukhin was detained in May 2026. In early August, his lawyer, Yuri Shel, said the treason charge stemmed from tax payments in Ukraine. At the time, it was unclear which tax the Russian authorities had taken issue with.
Officers from Russia’s Federal Security Service found records of the tax payments on Varyukhin’s phone during a search at the airport, his lawyer said.
Money transfers to support the Ukrainian army have previously led to treason prosecutions in Russia. But Varyukhin is the first person known to be prosecuted for treason for paying taxes into Ukraine’s state budget, Mediazona noted.

"As a result of the strikes… warehouse buildings are on fire, and residential buildings have been damaged. There may be people under the rubble of a residential building that was hit in the attack. A search and rescue operation is underway," he added.

Data publicării: 05.10.2026 14:17
Foto: Getty Images Urmărește Digi24 în Google Discover Adaugă Digi24 ca sursă preferată în Google
Trimisul României la Chișinău, Cristian-Leon Țurcanu, a condamnat cu fermitate atacul Rusiei asupra punctului de trecere a frontiereri Palanca, în urma căruia o persoană ar fost rănită. 
Misiunea diplomatică română de la Chișinău a transmis: „Condamnăm cu fermitate incidentul grav produs astăzi în zona Palanca, în urma căruia o persoană a fost rănită, pe fondul atacurilor Federației Ruse împotriva Ucrainei. Acesta survine după mai multe incidente cu drone înregistrate în ultimele zile, care au afectat spațiul aerian și securitatea Republicii Moldova.
Este o nouă dovadă clară a consecințelor directe pe care războiul de agresiune al Rusiei îl are asupra securității Republicii Moldova și asupra stabilității regionale.…

shrnuti: Russian attacks caused power outages in six oblasts on 5 October, as Ukrenergo repair crews work to restore power while avoiding nation-wide grid cuts.

vyrez.text:
Russian strikes cause power outages across six Ukrainian regions | Ukrainska Pravda
Stock photo: Getty Images
New power outages caused by Russian attacks have been recorded in Donetsk, Kharkiv, Sumy, Poltava, Odesa and Kherson oblasts as of the morning of 5 October.
Source: Ukrenergo , Ukraine's state-owned electricity transmission operator
Details: Emergency repair work has already begun where the security situation permits. Power engineers are repairing damaged equipment and re-establishing electricity supply to consumers.
Advertisement:





The company projects no electricity consumption restrictions on 5 October. Meanwhile, new Russian attacks could alter the situation in specific regions, so consumers are advised to monitor announcements from their local distribution network operators.
The company recommends shifting the use of high-power electrical appliances to the hours between 10:00 and 16:00, when industrial solar power plants operate most efficiently.
In the evening, from 17:00 to 22:00, citizens are asked not to turn on several high-power appliances simultaneously to reduce the load on equipment damaged by attacks.

shrnuti: Komentář: Vyjádření slovenského premiéra o bezpečných školách pouhý den po útoku ve Staškově naznačují, že ztráta kontroly je vážnější než jen politická.

Památník, který vznikl po útoku ve škole ve slovenském Staškově. Foto: Šimon Kern, Deník N
Komentář: Vyjádření slovenského premiéra o bezpečných školách pouhý den po útoku ve Staškově naznačují, že ztráta kontroly je vážnější než jen politická.
Více o poslechu Deníku N
Robert Fico měl v uplynulých dnech co dělat, aby udržel svou vládu. K tomu měl ještě záhadnou virózu, která se projevovala tak, že se ztrácel a potom překvapivě objevoval.
Odvolání ministra životního prostředí Tomáše Taraby a ponížení od předsedy SNS Andreje Danka v kombinaci s únavou asi způsobily, že premiér selhal nejen v kabinetní politice, ale i jako člověk.
Na tradičním setkání se studenty, tentokrát v Bánovcích nad Bebravou, řekl: „Neblázněme! Buďme rádi, že na Slovensku žijeme v klidu, že nám na hlavy nepadají rakety a naše děti mohou bezpečně chodit do školy.“ Řekl to jen den po útoku ve škole ve Staškově. V té době už byla mrtvá jedna učitelka a třináctiletá Nela byla v kritickém stavu. O den později zemřela i ona.
Ztratil kontrolu
Fico se ukázal jako bezcitný a sebestředný muž, který se při…

Aviation watchers such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers flying out of the base in Gloucestershire on Sunday.

Two Iranian men have been charged with terror offenses over an alleged plot to bomb Manchester’s Jewish community.
Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, appeared in a British court on Saturday on charges of preparing to commit an act of terrorism or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism.
Police said the two men, who were arrested last month on the eve of the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur, had received material and instructions on how to make a bomb, identified targets and carried out reconnaissance ahead of an attack on Jewish targets.

Italy’s Ustica enigma: Can French files solve mystery crash blamed on stray missile?
Analysis
Europe
France’s decision to share defence documents with the Italian judiciary has raised hopes of a breakthrough in investigations into the 1980 crash of a passenger jet near the island of Ustica, which a former Italian president claimed was mistakenly shot down by a French fighter jet. Sceptics caution that the files are unlikely to shed light on one of Italy’s most enduring mysteries, let alone reveal a culprit.

8 min Reading time

By:
Benjamin DODMAN
The reconstructed wreckage of Itavia Flight 870, which crashed near the island of Ustica in June 1980. © Emiliano Grillotti, AP
A rocky outpost of Italy in the Tyrrhenian Sea, the island of Ustica owes its name to the smouldering volcanic lava that gave its striking rock formations their dark hue.
For many Italians, however, the picturesque island is synonymous with a notorious plane crash that claimed 81 lives, and the intricate cover-up that buried its causes in a thick fog…

Russland intensiviert seine hybride Kriegsführung mitten in Europa und testet gezielt die roten Linien der NATO. Doch was passiert, wenn ein solcher Anschlag auf deutschem Boden tatsächlich gelingt und den Bündnisfall auslöst? Im Gespräch analysiert Carlo, warum Putin gerade jetzt risikofreudiger wird und weshalb Friedrich Merz in der deutschen Debatte als entscheidender Schutzwall für weitere Hilfen gilt. Skip to main content
A Ukrainian grandmother came to Kazakhstan to collect her grandson. Instead, she was detained at Russia’s request.
October 2, 2026, 4:26 pm
Source: Deutsche Welle
Ukrainian citizen Liubov Rozhanska was detained at Astana’s airport after arriving from Istanbul. She is now being held in a pretrial detention center, and a court hearing is expected within three days. Russia requested her detention through the Collective Security Treaty Organization , her lawyers told DW. Rozhanska could be extradited to Russia, where she is being investigated for child abduction.
Rozhanska had flown to Kazakhstan to pick up her grandson, who was to be brought there from Russia, lawyer Alexey Pryanishnikov said. The boy was born in 2018 during her daughter Alla Andreyeva’s first marriage. In 2021, his mother took him from Odesa to the Kaliningrad region to join her second husband. In 2022, she renounced her Ukrainian citizenship and her son’s, and both became Russian citizens.
In 2025, following a lawsuit filed by the boy’s father, Ukraine’s Supreme Court…

V aleriya Tkachenko was dropping her son off at school in central Kyiv when the air raid alert sounded. Staff hurried the children and parents into the shelter, where the frightened lawyer spent the next two hours with her son.
“I’m scared to death all day about what could happen to my son,” she said as she emerged from the shelter, already late for work.

NATO allies must be prepared for further hostile actions by Russia against the Alliance, and the response should be increased support for Ukraine.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said this during a visit to the headquarters of the 1st German-Netherlands Corps in Münster, according to Ukrinform.


Rutte said that Russia was repeatedly testing the Allies across Europe through airspace violations, arson, sabotage and the hybrid attack on Leipzig Airport in August. He noted that there was no direct military attack on NATO…

shrnuti: It comes as Western retailers face the risk of state asset seizures, which Putin defended as a response to the EU freezing its state funds.

Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder has joined the supervisory board of Hyperglobus, the Russian arm of the German superstore chain Globus, business media reported Friday.
The appointment comes as Western retailers face the risk of state asset seizures, which President Vladimir Putin defended as a response to the EU freezing its state funds.
Hyperglobus owner Thomas Bruch praised Schröder as an “ideal addition” who would help maintain a “dialogue-oriented approach” in Russia, according to a statement published by Kommersant.
Schröder was quoted emphasizing the importance of maintaining economic ties and investing in Russia’s food sector. He will be responsible for supporting the strategic development of the business, RBC cited the company as saying.

Když roste tlak, Vladimir Putin znovu vytahuje svou nejsilnější kartu: jaderné zbraně. Včera varoval, že případný přímý útok na Rusko – a explicitně zmínil Kaliningradskou oblast – by okamžitě otevřel otázku nasazení „všech zbraní“, které má Moskva k dispozici.
Trefa Vlastilava Břízy Video: Novinky
Článek
Pak sáhl po známé dramaturgické metafoře Antona Pavloviče Čechova - když v prvním dějství visí na zdi puška, nakonec vystřelí. V souvislosti s jadernými zbraněmi mrazivá slova. Putin zároveň dodal, že právě tomu je třeba zabránit.
Obdobná varování nejsou nová. Moskva sahá po jaderné rétorice opakovaně, zvláště když roste tlak kolem války na Ukrajině. A její cíl? Znejistit Západ. Vystrašit ho. Přimět ho přemýšlet, kam až může v podpoře Kyjeva zajít, aniž překročí ruskou červenou linii.
Jaderné zbraně totiž nemusí explodovat, aby fungovaly. Stačí…

titulek: Mistaken for drone: Russian Su-35 fighter shoots down Mi-8 helicopter in friendly fire
titulekPuvodni: Mistaken for drone: Russian Su-35 fighter shoots down Mi-8 helicopter in friendly fire
shrnuti: A Russian Su-35 fighter jet reportedly shot down a Russian Mi-8 helicopter in Voronezh Oblast after mistaking it for a Ukrainian drone, killing three crew members.

vyrez.text:
Russian Su-35 shoots down Russian Mi-8 after mistaking it for Ukrainian drone | Ukrainska Pravda
A Russian Su-35 multirole fighter jet has shot down a Russian Mi-8 helicopter. Three crew members aboard the helicopter were killed in the incident, which occurred on 1 October.
Source: Taras Hryhorovych Reports on Telegram
Details: The incident first became known on the evening of 1 October. Several sources reported it, including the Exilenova+ Telegram channel, which reports information on Russian equipment losses, citing sources within the Russian military.
Advertisement:





Initial reports indicated that a Russian military helicopter had crashed in Voronezh Oblast. No further details were disclosed at the time. Exilenova+ reported the following day that the helicopter had supposedly been shot down by Russian air defence. The channel later stated that it had in fact been downed by a Russian Su-35 fighter jet after the Mi-8 was mistaken for a Ukrainian drone.



Su-35 multirole fighter jet




Background:
On 29 September, Russia's Defence Ministry also reported that a military aircraft had crashed in Russia's Amur Oblast. The ministry claimed that the crash had occurred…

titulekPuvodni: Media reveal information about Russian who may have organised sabotage at Leipzig airport
shrnuti: Russian biker Oleg Lyovushkin, who has ties to a Russian military intelligence officer, may have organised an attempted sabotage at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany.

vyrez.text:

Photo: Getty Images
Russian biker Oleg Lyovushkin, who is linked to a Russian military intelligence officer, may have organised an attempted sabotage at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany.
Source: a joint investigation by The Telegraph and Welt am Sonntag, as reported by European Pravda
Details: According to the investigation, Lyovushkin presumably organised the attempt to plant explosives at the airport. German investigators believe that Belarusian intermediary agent Andrei Karshakov was supposed to carry out the plan.
Advertisement:





Journalists analysed intelligence documents from Germany, Lithuania, and Poland, and also spoke with representatives of Western secret services. According to their data, Lyovushkin and Karshakov arrived in Germany to carry out the sabotage operation.
German investigators suspect that Lyovushkin conducted reconnaissance of the airport shortly before the attack, after which he instructed Karshakov to execute the plan.
Investigators also found similarities between the incident in Leipzig and other attempted Russian sabotage operations in…

Letecký útok na Pearl Harbor je pro Američany stále trauma. Což je patrné i z děje nové knihy Danielle Steelové Létající andělé. Pro našince je zase traumatem Mnichov 1938. Právě v této době se odehrává příběh mladé dívky Josefíny v díle Štěpána Javůrka. Básník Rainer Maria Rilke stále patří k oblíbeným autorům, což bezpochyby podpoří i jeho sbírka básní Okna plná dálek. Dále máme v nabídce publikaci o historii Krakonoše, atlas plazů i knihu věnující se jednomu tabuizovanému tématu, totiž bolesti.

Zatímco se vyrovnávají se svým zármutkem, sílí jejich odhodlání sehrát ve válečném úsilí významnou roli. BERLIN — If the explosive had actually detonated, investigators might not have gotten their clearest look yet at what European officials believe is a wider Russian campaign of attacks.
On Aug. 4, a drone struck the wing of a Ukrainian aircraft at Germany’s Leipzig Airport and fell onto the tarmac. Strapped beneath it was a tin can packed with explosives. The device remained intact.
That gave investigators something unusually valuable: the bomb itself. The can was sealed with a metal plate stamped with seven circular indentations, according to an investigative file from German federal police reviewed by the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network.
Advertisement
It wasn’t the first time such an improvised explosive had been discovered on European soil. Almost two years earlier, on Aug. 20, 2024, police investigators arrived at a cemetery in Kaunas, Lithuania, with a bomb disposal team. Seven people were killed in an explosion at a chemical plant in Russia’s Moscow region, the Telegram news channel Shot reported , as emergency crews responded to a fire at the facility.
The blast hit the Krasnozavodsk Chemical Plant, which produces ammunition and pyrotechnics, according to publicly available information. Authorities had not commented on the incident, and the reported death toll remained unconfirmed.
Shot reported that the seven people were inside workshop No. 4, which collapsed completely. Survivors said more workers had been inside, the channel reported, adding that rescue operations were continuing.
The Telegram channel Mash, citing local residents, reported three powerful explosions that shook nearby homes before a fire broke out. More than 40 workers were at the plant at the time, and an evacuation was underway, it said.

UK-Iran national arrested under Terrorism Act over RAF Fairford incident
Counter-terrorism police arrest 27-year-old in Westminster, while second man questioned under caution
Detectives have arrested a dual UK-Iranian national on suspicion of terrorism offences as part of an investigation into a suspected plot near RAF Fairford.
Counter-terrorism police said the 27-year-old man was arrested on Thursday in Westminster on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006.
A second man, 26, who is a UK national, has been questioned under caution.
Five men in their 20s were arrested in the village of Whelford, Gloucestershire, outside the RAF base in the early hours of Sunday after police were alerted to suspicious vans in the area. They were released on police bail.

EU chce rychleji a koordinovaněji reagovat na ruské hybridní útoky. Ministři zahraničí se začátkem týdne v Bruselu začali zabývat novým mechanismem, který jim k tomu má dopomoci. Šéfka unijní diplomacie Kaja Kallasová zároveň varovala, že Rusko sabotážní operace v Evropě plánuje neustále a v nejbližší době nepřestane.
Foto: Getty Images
Šéfka unijní diplomacie Kaja Kallasová
Článek
Nový „nouzový bezpečnostní mechanismus“ má umožnit rychlou koordinaci ve chvíli, kdy některá členská země zaznamená hybridní útok. Zástupci zemí se sešli v pondělí, aby zkoordinovali svou reakci. Podle Kallasové jde o situace, které sice nedosahují úrovně ozbrojeného útoku, přesto ale vyžadují společnou evropskou reakci.
„Musíme být ostražití, protože ze zpravodajských informací vyplývá, že Rusko plánuje další sabotážní akce,“ uvedla podle serveru Euronews .
Ačkoli diplomaté uvádějí, že podrobnosti o tom, co by…

Smrt dívky oznámil ve slovenském parlamentu jeho předseda Richard Raši. Poslanci poté uctili památku oběti minutou ticha.
Nelku po útoku v kritickém stavu převezli vrtulníkem do nemocnice v Martině. Podle webu tn.live.sk ji měl útočník třikrát bodnout a v důsledku ztráty velkého množství krve utrpěla hemoragický šok. Musela se podrobit několika operacím, ale lékaři ji už nedokázali zachránit.
Při útoku byla zraněna také 44letá učitelka, která je ve stabilizovaném stavu.
Útočníka ze slovenské základky vychovávali prarodiče, matka byla v těžké životní situaci

Ve slovenské sněmovně to ve čtvrtek řekl předseda parlamentu Richard Raši (Hlas), poslanci dívku následně uctili minutou ticha. Podezřelý z útoku není kvůli nízkému věku trestně odpovědný. Umístěn byl do příslušného detenčního ústavu.

France, Germany, Britain, Italy, Ireland and the European Commission joined the talks to decide how to respond to pressure from Washington to draw down oil stockpiles or face a ban on U.S. exports of diesel, three European officials told POLITICO.

BRUSSELS — A Russian bombing attack on a European weapons factory should trigger NATO's Article 5 mutual defense clause, the EU's top defense official said Thursday.
The call comes in the wake of a growing number of suspicious incidents at arms factories across Europe, some of which have been attributed to Russia.
"If Russia will hit our factories in European territories, that would be Article 5," European Defense Commissioner Andrius Kubilius told Polish television on the margins of a meeting of the European Parliament's Defence and Security Committee.

The remarks come after Russian foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova on Wednesday warned that "weapons factories in European countries that produce arms for Ukraine are potential military targets for Russia."
NATO chief Mark Rutte this week issued a strong rebuke of Moscow after Russia sent a note to the alliance threatening nuclear escalation over NATO activity near its border.

PARIS — French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu called an emergency meeting on Thursday to address the fast-growing number of student protests across the country.
The movement, which was born of anger over conditions in secondary schools, began in recent days with teenagers blocking entrances to educational institutions in underprivileged suburbs of Paris.
The Union Syndicale Lycéenne , the student union spearheading the demonstrations, said they want authorities to address a “shortage of teachers and staff, dilapidated high schools, overcrowded classrooms, and overloaded schedules.”
Advertisement
While the protests have been largely peaceful, some have seen trash cans set on fire outside school entrances and buildings vandalized.
The head of the greater Paris region, Valérie Pécresse, said Thursday that more than 200 schools were affected and the damage had exceeded €1 million, Le Monde reported . Protesters and their supporters have accused the police of using excessive force to disperse gatherings.

The Police and Border Guard Board confirmed the detention of the ship.

At the same time, Russia, Estonia and Finland have an agreement that ships may pass through that location, because that route is safer for large vessels than sailing between the shallows in Estonia's maritime area.

On Latvian Public Media (LSM), content in Russian will only be permitted in exceptional circumstances, in the event of a state of emergency, or for the specific purpose of countering disinformation. This was decided by the Saeima on Thursday, 1 October.
55 MPs voted ‘for’, whilst 24 voted ‘against’.
Latvian Television and Latvian Radio do not broadcast in Russian, but the LSM.lv portal still produces content in Russian.
Until now, public media had been obliged to produce programmes in minority languages, but following the Constitutional Court’s (ST) judgement, this situation had to change, as the court ruled that LSM’s content must primarily be in Latvian, whilst the Russian language is self-sufficient in the Latvian media, and therefore the state need not take special care of it.
